page: Vultr voc-m-8c-64gb-1600s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server powered by an AMD EPYC processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this instance features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core, running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The processor includes 32 MB of L3 cache and supports hardware features such as AVX, AES cryptography, and SHA_NI. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Local storage is bundled with 1600 GB of NVMe SSD capacity, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU accelerators are present.

Benchmark evaluations reveal strong memory performance and exceptional single-core capabilities. In stress-ng single-core CPU testing, the server achieves a top-tier score of 3135.58, placing it in the top 10% of tested instances. Large-block memory bandwidth benchmarks show strong performance in the top 25%, with read speeds of 258.36 GB/sec and write speeds of 152.63 GB/sec. Multi-core CPU performance, software compilation, and database operations fall within the average tier. However, the server exhibits weaker performance in LLM inference prompt processing for medium 7B models, scoring 21.78 tokens/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the server offers a high-density memory profile and substantial NVMe storage capacity relative to its 8-vCPU compute allocation. This resource distribution makes it highly suitable for memory-intensive workloads that do not require massive parallel compute scaling. Recommended workloads include relational databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, medium-scale web serving, and general-purpose enterprise applications requiring fast local storage and high memory capacity.
